title: The 1933 band's choir singing and the viper's language of Sweet Sue
summary: Randolph had the band singing like Fred Waring's Pennsylvanians; Sweet Sue was Budd Johnson's idea, with Armstrong interpreting viper talk.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah, that was an awful good band, that '33 band.

That '33 -- but I had a band --oh, but you haven't gottento that yet. I'll tell you about that band. That band was something else. It was the band that -- I think it was Walter Winchell said, (unintelligible) Louis Armstrong and his band. And I had out of that band singing like Fred Waring and his Pennsylvanians.
Well they do some (unintelligible) singing here, the
Basin Street Blues. They do a choir background with Louis scatting.
Now, you also did -- I think maybe at a later session, 'Sweet Sue,' which is a very funny record. Whose idea was that?

Now, that was Bud Johnson's. And of course, Louis would say -- no, Bud Johnson would say, (musical sounds), and Louis would interpret it, say -- they call themselves talking the viper mixer's language.
Do they say viper's mixer's language on there?
Yeah, that's the viper mixer's language.
Well, there were tempo changes and all of that. Was that your doing or did the guys just work it among you, or how?
We just worked that out among us. We'd say -- yes, uh-huh.
